outcome: A detach function releases only the attachment it was returned for. After the page has torn the client down with `destroy()` and mounted again on the same client with a fresh `dataLayer()`, running the stale detach from the first mount changes nothing the page can see: `layer.push` keeps the identity it had, the live attachment still captures the next push to the transport exactly once, and the page's array still holds one entry per push. The live mount's own detach still works — the page's own push comes back by identity and the transport is silent afterwards. A stale declarative detach is inert in the same way: the live scan keeps its one registration on the element and keeps reporting the click, and the live declarative detach removes it.
